newsitem.title: USA: Transocean sees weak results, stock falls.
newsitem.headline: Transocean sees weak results, stock falls.

text.p: Transocean Offshore Inc. Monday made a fourth-quarter earnings forecast that disappointed Wall Street, triggering a sell-off in its stock.
The offshore drilling company's stock tumbled $5.25 to $60.25 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was among the most active issues in early afternoon trading.

Transocean, which changed its name from Sonat Offshore Drilling Inc. in September, estimated that earnings per share for the quarter ended Dec. 31 would be about 15 cents to 20 cents below analysts' average forecast of 55 cents.

In the 1995 quarter, the Houston-based company earned $11.1 million, or 39 cents a share, on revenues of $83.1 million. Final results for the fourth quarter and full year will be announced on Feb. 18.
Transocean said the earnings shortfall was mainly due to higher operating expenses for repair and replacements on certain North Sea rigs that cost $3 million to $4 million in the quarter.
High startup costs on two rigs resulted in an estimated operating loss of $3.6 million during the period.
A weak performance in the company's U.S. Gulf of Mexico operation led to an estimated operating loss of $4.7 million.

Losses were recorded on four wells due to operating difficulties that delayed completion of the projects, the company said. Two of these wells remain in progress and were expected to be completed in February 1997.
Transocean has initiated changes in its U.S. Gulf of Mexico organisation that should improve performance, the company said without providing details.
